subject: Scale AI news
text:

With Meta's $15B deal with ScaleAI, there's growing urgency around scalable, high-quality data infrastructure - & as we're seeing a wave of strong inbound demand - thought i'd reach out to explore if we can help in a similar way.

subject: [COMPANY] & Ecnord - In-house DataOps Infra
text:
Hi [NAME],

Sorry we didn't get a chance to connect at CVPR this year. At the booth we
caught up with one of our customers Actuate AI who we recently helped
migrate aways from their legacy in-house data curation/annotation tooling
-- they were finding it hard to iterate on their video surveillance models
for various threat detection use cases (similar to [COMPANY] Watch). If I'm not
mistaken [COMPANY] has also relied on in-house to date?

We're now mostly assisting with improving their labelling efficiency
(autolabelling using SAM2, tracking algos, agentic integrations for
pre-labelling etc.) & overall pipeline integration (i.e. tightly coupled
data curation/annotation workflows) -- with the goal of speeding up their
model iteration cycles & freeing up their engineers previously spent
maintaining DataOps infra that's not a core part of their IP.

Not sure how familiar you are with Encord - we're a data development
platform built for advanced computer vision and multimodal AI teams to
build better models (~5 years old, 70+ employees, and $50M+ in funding).

Would you be open to a quick intro call? I can share how we're supporting
others in your space - Thursday/Friday mornings are usually pretty free.

subject: Skydio's MLOps solution
text:
Hi [NAME], hope you're keeping well.

I spoke with [SENDER] Higgins a few weeks ago about Manna's computer vision
efforts and how that focus is likely to grow as you expand geographically -
particularly with the easing of US commercial drone regulations and new
partnerships like Deliveroo (congrats by the way).

Following Meta's $15B deal with Scale AI, we've seen a sharp uptick in
interest around scalable, high-quality data infrastructure - especially
from UAV teams. We're working with ML teams at companies like Skydio,
Zipline, and Drone AG to streamline data curation, annotation, and model
evaluation - helping them move faster, improve model performance, and
reduce engineering lift.

I reached out to [SENDER] to grab a coffee while I'm back in Dublin tomorrow
(in from London), but I believe he's out of office - so I thought I'd check
if you might be up for a chat?

text:

be open to a quick chat next week? I'm usually free Thurs/Fri mornings.

subject: [Encord] Accelerate model iteration with edge case data curation
text:
Hi [NAME],

Congratulations on the recent launch of the VISION FVR-Mark4 - I'd imagine
this has increased the collection of in-field data?

We recently started working with Automotus, who also produce very similar
models to Flash (permit matching, car counting, etc.), and they had
problems with data visualization across hundreds of thousands of hours of
driving data. So I thought I'd reach out to see if you're encountering
similar challenges at Flash?

We enabled them, along with other mobility companies' AI teams (Woven by
Toyota, Metropolis, etc.), to curate data across hundreds of millions of
multimodal files (image, video, IR), using metadata filtering, similarity
search, embedding visualization, etc. In turn, they were better able to
identify edge cases to annotate and iterate, and build more accurate models
faster.

platform built for advanced computer vision and multimodal AI teams to

subject: Data Visualization at scale: Encord / Metropolis
text:
Hi [NAME],

Congratulations on the recent partnership with Dayton Airport - I'd imagine
this has increased the collection of in-field data once again?

We recently started working with Automotus, who also produce very similar
models to Metropolis (permit matching, car counting, etc.), and they had
problems with data visualization across hundreds of thousands of hours of
driving data. So I thought I'd reach out to see if you're encountering
similar challenges at Metropolis?

We enabled them, along with other mobility companies' AI teams (Woven by
Toyota, Metropolis, etc.), to curate data across hundreds of millions of
multimodal files (image, video), using metadata filtering, similarity
search, embedding visualization, etc. In turn, they were better able to
identify edge cases to annotate and iterate, and build more accurate models
faster.

Not sure how familiar you are with Encord - we're a data development
platform built for advanced computer vision and multimodal AI teams to
build better models (~5 years old, 100+ employees, and $50M+ in funding).

Would you be open to a quick intro call this week or next? I'm usually
pretty free Thursday/Friday mornings but happy to flex as needed.
